timeline.summary: Mikey narrates a public wedding-day encounter with Jackson Wang, shows the bride's post and comments, and interprets the phrase 'real husband' as evidence of attraction and dissatisfaction.
He introduces social proof: women supposedly value men already recognized by other women, using school and group-status examples.
Public figures and male status hierarchies are used to argue that attention concentrates on visible winners and that facts matter less than feelings.
He proposes 'excitement transfer,' claiming arousal created by one man can be redirected to another, supported by a nightclub anecdote.
He develops a lover-provider binary and claims many women marry for support while desiring higher-status men.
A personal sexual anecdote is used to make genetic-preference claims; he also states that he continued to use condoms for safety.
He returns to the identifiable bride and husband, speculating about housing, bride price, gold, status, resentment and future marital dynamics.
He closes by saying men should understand social proof and avoid being reduced to a material provider.

examples.summary: A bride's public post, photos with Jackson Wang, a highlighted 'real husband' phrase and surrounding comments are used to infer sexual and marital motives that the images themselves do not establish.
School leaders, sports captains and celebrities illustrate the social-proof thesis, while a nightclub story is used to claim excitement transfer.
Later posts, memes and dramatized relationship clips accompany speculation about the husband and marriage; they are not direct evidence from the couple.

visual_findings: All 18 sparse frames and 61 targeted dense frames were reviewed. Dense windows cover 55-130 and 690-735 seconds at two-second intervals; contact sheets are preserved beside the extracted frames.

The early dense window shows wedding footage, photos with Jackson Wang, the bride's public post and highlighted comments including the 'real husband' wording. It verifies what the edit displays, not the narrator's claims about arousal, marriage motives or dissatisfaction.
The later dense window shows commentary posts, memes, studio narration and dramatized relationship clips. It does not show the couple's financial documents, private communications or direct account.
Some usernames and public-profile details remain visible in the archived frames, so user-facing reuse would require privacy review and minimization.
No continuous original audio-visual review was performed; dense sampling cannot establish the completeness, date or source chain of the public-post material.

permissions.reason: The source relies on identifiable public-post material, private-motive speculation, unsupported gender and evolutionary claims, and a reductive lover-provider model.

limitations: Automatic transcript was not checked word-for-word against original audio and may corrupt names, slang and quoted post text.
The public post may be humorous, parasocial or context-specific; it cannot establish sexual intent or marital dissatisfaction.
Dense frame review is discontinuous and does not authenticate the post's source chain or completeness.
The social-proof and excitement-transfer models are supported only by selected examples and anecdotes in this source.
No evidence is provided for the couple's finances, sexual relationship, paternity, future behavior or motives.
